description: The Lectio Edition of Genesis: the plainest prose in the Bible, in plain current English that keeps its refrains and leaves its puzzles open.
what: The first book of the Bible. Eleven chapters about everyone: creation, a garden, a murder, a flood, a tower. Then thirty-nine about one family: Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob, Leah and Rachel, Joseph and his brothers.
why_title: The Hebrew is plain. Four hundred years of English have made it grand.
why: Genesis is spare. The Hebrew has a small vocabulary, repeats itself on purpose, and almost never explains. It says what happened and leaves the judgment to the reader.

The King James Version of 1611 is one of the great works of English, and it adds a solemnity the Hebrew does not have. It also varies words the Hebrew repeats. Abraham answers "Here I am" three times in one chapter, to God, to his son, and to the messenger who stops the knife. The King James gives it three ways.
The Lectio Edition keeps the refrains word for word, keeps more of the Hebrew's "and" than modern taste likes, and leaves a puzzle as a puzzle. The King James stays in the app beside it.
status: In the app, the King James is still what opens by default for Genesis. The Lectio Edition is complete, all fifty chapters. It is a beta, and it becomes the default after the readers' review and the editor's read.
choices_lede: These rules come from the charter written for the biblical books and from the review.
choices: Where the Hebrew is unknown or can be read two ways, the edition prints the received text and leaves it open. A scholar's guess goes in a note, not in the verse. "Gopher wood" stays "gopher wood". Nobody knows what it was.
Refrains and repeated words are the same each time.
The divine name is "the LORD" in capitals, the convention English Bibles have used since Tyndale. It marks that a substitution is being made.
*Shamayim* is "sky" for the physical sky and "heaven" where it is God's place or title.
The poems inside Genesis are verse and should be set as lines. The build cannot do that yet. See below.

divergences.older: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." (King James)
divergences.lectio: When God began to create the heavens and the earth
divergences.why: The Hebrew most likely opens a clause that runs on to "God said, Let there be light". Creation starts with a scene already dark and wet. Rashi read it this way in the eleventh century.
The Hebrew is a rhyming pair. In the same verse *ruach* is breath, wind and spirit at once, and the edition has "the breath of God hovered".
*Ezer* is used most often of God and implies no lower rank. *Kenegdo* means his counterpart.

divergences.older: "Get thee out of thy country" (King James)
divergences.why: Two blunt Hebrew words. The verse begins "Go". Everything after it follows from a man obeying an order that gives no reason.

divergences.older: "the LORD made a covenant with Abram" (King James)
divergences.lectio: the LORD cut a covenant with Abram
divergences.why: The Hebrew idiom is to cut a covenant, and here it is literal. Animals are cut in half and fire passes between the pieces. "Made" hides the knife.

divergences.older: "Behold, here I am", "Here am I" (King James)
divergences.why: One word, three times. It is the spine of the chapter. Varying it breaks it.
The word occurs only here. The picture is most likely the ramp of a temple tower, a fixed way between the sky and a stone in open country.

checked: the King James Version (1611). The Hebrew is not in the bundle, so readings of the Hebrew came from the reviewing model's own knowledge of the text.
review_note: The figures above cover chapters 1 to 34, which were reviewed with the other works. Chapters 35 to 50 were drafted the same night and read by one reader: 15 graded A and 1 graded B, with six small fixes applied. That reader asked that its Hebrew readings be confirmed against a printed text.
open: The editor's own read of all fifty chapters. Until then the King James remains the default.
The poems (2:23, 3:14 to 19, 4:23 to 24, 9:25 to 27, 25:23, 27:27 to 29, 27:39 to 40, and chapter 49) are still set as prose. The build has to learn to keep line breaks inside a paragraph first.

Notes for the places left open: gopher wood, who gave the tenth at 14:20, the reading at 16:13, Joseph's coat, the traders at 37:28, "until Shiloh comes" at 49:10, and others. They have not been written.
The Hebrew readings for chapters 35 to 50 should be confirmed against a printed text.
